title: Peas and corn, cooked, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: Peas and corn, cooked with added fat, are a blend of boiled green peas and sweet corn sautéed in a small amount of vegetable oil. This combination is commonly used in side dishes, soups, and salads, providing a pleasant flavor, soft texture, and an extra source of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Peas and corn are often paired in traditional dishes worldwide, such as the American "corn and pea medley."
Corn contains carotenoids that give it a yellow hue, while peas are rich in plant protein.
Cooking with fat enhances flavor and helps absorb the fat‑soluble vitamins found in corn.
The mixture retains most B‑vitamins, which are important for energy metabolism.
Heat treatment makes peas softer and easier to digest.

items.title: Rich source of plant protein
items.content: Peas provide about 5 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains complex carbohydrates
items.content: Both corn and peas supply slowly digestible carbs, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of vitamin C and carotenoids
items.content: Corn supplies vitamin C and carotenoids (lutein, zeaxanthin) beneficial for vision and immunity.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from peas promotes intestinal motility and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Fat as a nutrient carrier
items.content: Added vegetable fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins A and E present in corn.

items.title: Allergy to legumes or corn
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to peas or corn.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The added fat increases the product’s caloric content; portion control is advisable.

items.title: Presence of phytic acid
items.content: Peas contain phytic acid, which can reduce mineral absorption when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Sodium content in prepared mix
items.content: If the product is seasoned with salt, total dietary sodium should be considered.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve peas and corn as a side dish with meat, fish, or tofu, stir them into soups, stews, and salads. They reheat well in the microwave or on a skillet. For a lighter taste, choose an unsalted version.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the cooked mixture in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags; when reheating, bring to an internal temperature of at least 75 °C.
